organization.name: Community Resource Network
organization.mission: To rescue surplus food and usable items for redistribution to organizations and families in need in our communities, to reduce and prevent waste, and to encourage better management of the surplus that would otherwise end up in landfills.

coreValues.title: Resourcefulness
coreValues.description: Making the most of every donation
points: We saved more than 2.2 million pounds of unsalable grocery and household items from general disposal last year.
We consistently serve over 500 households in the greater Puget Sound area.
Our 100% volunteer structure and business model provide economical, streamlined services without burdening taxpayers.
Our volunteer members become adept at utilizing and repurposing a wide variety of items that would otherwise be tossed.

coreValues.title: Environmental Responsibility
coreValues.description: Protecting our planet through thoughtful distribution
points: CRN is committed to the thoughtful distribution of all usable donations that we receive.
Inedible grocery items are utilized by local farmers and gardeners before being considered for city/county compost.
Packaging from inedible grocery donations is separated out for reuse or recycling.
Returned, damaged or shopworn items are distributed or repurposed before being considered for recycling or disposal.

coreValues.title: Personal Responsibility & Growth
points: Our volunteer members are acutely aware of the ripple effect created through meeting basic human needs. Each need we meet frees up resources for meeting other needs in our community and in the world.
Many of our volunteer members receive a portion of the donations. These volunteer members show up consistently to work hard and realize the great value of their labor.

coreValues.title: Reliability
coreValues.description: Consistent service you can count on
points: Our teams process donations 7 days a week including major holidays.
Our teams process donations during inclement weather.
We accept virtually any item offered by our donating partners.
We maintain records of donations and can supply the record to donors for tax purposes.
Our volunteer members realize the strength of a committed team effort and are particularly reliable in fulfilling their assigned duties for the organization.
Our volunteer members willingly support and fill in for one another when calendar conflicts, sickness or emergencies arise.

coreValues.title: Dignity
points: Many of our beneficiaries are isolated, reluctant to ask for help or overlooked by other organized distribution systems. By identifying and delivering necessities to such families/individuals, CRN volunteer members make a personal connection that conveys dignity and worth.
Our volunteer members may receive a portion of donations. These volunteer members work diligently and preserve personal dignity through the sense of 'earning' through service.

volunteer.intro: CRN is run entirely by committed, trained volunteer members who complete all operational tasks.
tasks: Transporting donations to CRN distribution centers
Delivering goods to targeted communities, organizations and households
Cleaning and maintaining CRN distribution centers
Generating and recording reports at the conclusion of each volunteer shift
volunteer.schedule: Volunteer members commit to working 3-5 scheduled hours per week.

contributing.title: Contributing Partners
contributing.description: CRN currently partners with more than a dozen Puget Sound area chain and independent businesses. These businesses positively impact the local community by granting CRN to be a conduit to the community, distributing items they generously and thoughtfully donate.
contributing.note: Contributing partners have peace of mind to donate generously since the Bill Emerson Good Samaritan Food Donation Act limits liability of good faith donors.

receiving.title: Receiving Partners
receiving.description: CRN currently partners with local communities and organizations.

financial.title: Financial Partners
financial.description: CRN has NO paid staff. Our volunteer members accomplish every task necessary to fulfill our purpose.
financial.note: Our streamlined business model ensures that monetary donations are directed toward essential operating expenses, not salaries. We make the most of every dollar just as we make the most of every tomato, every orange, every egg, and every brussel sprout.

about.whoWeAre: CRN is a 501(c)3 non-profit volunteer organization established in 1998 and serves the greater Puget Sound area.
about.acknowledgement: Community Resource Network acknowledges that we gather and serve on the traditional territory of Coast Salish peoples, who have stewarded this land since time immemorial. We honor their enduring presence and the ongoing relationship between the Coast Salish people and this land.
about.specialThanks: We wish to thank Kaeden Brinkman for his creativity, dedication, and generosity in building the CRN website.
